record.original_question: In the setting of Theorem 3.5, let Omega be a C^{3,1} smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domain in C^n, let phi belong to C^{3,1}(partial Omega), and let u be the unique plurisubharmonic function on Omega, continuous up to the boundary, solving (dd^c u)^n = f in Omega with f >= 0 and f^{1/n} in C^{1,1}(closure Omega). Determine the minimal assumptions under which u belongs to C^2(closure Omega).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain with boundary of class $C^{3,1}$, let $\varphi \in C^{3,1}(\partial\Omega)$, and let $f \geq 0$ be a function on $\Omega$ such that $f^{1/n} \in C^{1,1}(\overline{\Omega})$. By a known result, there exists a unique plurisubharmonic function $u \in C(\overline{\Omega})$ solving the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge–Ampère equation
$$(dd^c u)^n = f \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = \varphi \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
and moreover $u \in C^{1,1}(\overline{\Omega})$. Here $d = \partial + \bar\partial$ and $d^c = i(\bar\partial - \partial)$, so $(dd^c u)^n$ is interpreted as a positive Borel measure (which under the stated regularity is absolutely continuous with bounded density).

Determine the minimal regularity assumptions on the domain $\Omega$, the boundary data $\varphi$, and the right-hand side $f$ under which the solution $u$ belongs to $C^2(\overline{\Omega})$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (including 2025–2026 papers on a priori estimates after Krylov and on Hölder/C^{1,1} regularity for the complex Monge–Ampère equation) continues to investigate regularity of solutions to the Dirichlet problem on strictly pseudoconvex domains. The standard known result yields C^{1,1} regularity under the stated hypotheses, while C^{2,α} estimates require stronger assumptions on the data. No source found establishes a sharp characterization of minimal assumptions guaranteeing C^2 up to the boundary, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A priori estimates for the complex Monge-Ampère equation after Krylov
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work revisiting Krylov's a priori estimates and C^{1,1} regularity for the complex Monge–Ampère equation on strictly pseudoconvex domains.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on regularity beyond C^{1,1} for complex Monge-Ampère, indicating the minimal-assumption C^2 question is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Hölder regularity of Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge–Ampère equation
status_evidence.snippet: 2026 paper studying Hölder regularity for the Dirichlet problem of the complex Monge-Ampère equation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2026) work still focuses on Hölder/below-C^2 regularity, supporting that the C^2 question remains open.
